key_decisions.decision: Baud generator structure and divider semantics
key_decisions.ma_choice: One shared free-running 16x tick generator for TX and RX; baud_div = clock cycles per 16x tick, round(f_clk/(16*baud)).
key_decisions.plan_choice: Integer divider in clk cycles per 16x tick, one shared tick generator; TX advances one bit every 16 ticks.

key_decisions.ma_choice: No clock-frequency parameter in RTL; only the runtime baud_div input.
key_decisions.plan_choice: Runtime divider input of parameterized width; no clock-frequency constant.
key_decisions.note: Spec forbids hard-coding the clock but does not exclude a CLK_FREQ reset default; both chose divider-only.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Fixed 16-bit baud_div (about 95 baud minimum at 100 MHz).
key_decisions.plan_choice: DIV_WIDTH parameter, sized to cover 9600 baud at 100 MHz.
key_decisions.note: Parameterizing the width is a minor variation. The structure is the same.

key_decisions.decision: Divider edge handling (zero value, runtime change)
key_decisions.ma_choice: 0 is treated as 1. A >= comparison tolerates a runtime decrease. baud_div is not latched, and firmware must change it only while !tx_busy && !rx_busy.
key_decisions.plan_choice: The 0/1 case is either clamped or held idle (left open). A mid-frame change takes effect at the next tick reload, with no latching.
key_decisions.note: The plan has the same unlatched behaviour but leaves the zero-divider policy undecided and has no busy-gated firmware rule.

key_decisions.ma_choice: 2-FF synchronizer reset to 1, then a 3-sample majority vote at mid-bit (ticks 6-8). No continuous debounce filter.
key_decisions.plan_choice: 2-FF synchronizer, then a 3-sample majority vote at ticks 7/8/9 for every bit.
key_decisions.note: The sample-tick offset differs by one and is not architectural.

key_decisions.ma_choice: A low on idle enters START. The mid-start majority is re-checked, and if it reads 1 the receiver returns to IDLE with nothing pushed.
key_decisions.plan_choice: A falling edge arms the receiver, which aborts to IDLE if the voted mid-start sample is high.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Errored bytes are still delivered. The RX FIFO is 10 bits wide ({parity_err, frame_err, data}) and the flags come out as RX stream sideband.
key_decisions.plan_choice: Same 10-bit FIFO entries, with sideband flags on the RX stream.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Drop the incoming byte and preserve FIFO contents. Sticky rx_overrun is cleared by a status_clr pulse, and clear wins over a simultaneous set.
key_decisions.plan_choice: Drop the incoming byte. Sticky rx_overflow is cleared by an rx_overflow_clr input, plus an extra one-cycle pulse output. The clear/set collision is to be defined.
key_decisions.note: The plan adds a pulse output, which is a minor interface addition.

key_decisions.ma_choice: BREAK state after a bad stop bit waits for the line to go high. A break gives one 0x00 entry with frame_err and no break flag.
key_decisions.plan_choice: Wait for rxd high before re-arming. A break shows up as a single 0x00 with frame_err and no break flag.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Push at the mid-stop-bit sample and leave STOP early, so start detection re-arms early to absorb baud mismatch.
key_decisions.plan_choice: The stop bit is sampled at mid-bit and the byte plus flags are pushed then, without waiting for the full stop bit.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Shared parity_en/parity_odd inputs, latched per frame by each FSM.
key_decisions.plan_choice: Shared parity_en/parity_odd, latched at frame start by each FSM.

key_decisions.ma_choice: FIFO-fed FSM with a registered txd and back-to-back frames (STOP goes directly to START with no idle gap).
key_decisions.plan_choice: Registered txd; the next start bit follows the stop bit immediately when the FIFO is non-empty.

key_decisions.ma_choice: tx_level/rx_level plus tx_busy/rx_busy outputs. Busy is used to gate safe baud changes.
key_decisions.plan_choice: Full/empty/count FIFO status outputs; no busy indicators.
key_decisions.note: Levels match. The missing busy signals weaken the safe-reconfiguration story, but the core structure is unaffected.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Synchronous FWFT FIFOs, FIFO_DEPTH parameter defaulting to 8 (power of 2), used for both directions.
key_decisions.plan_choice: FIFO_DEPTH parameter defaulting to 8 for both FIFOs; RX data held stable while stalled.
key_decisions.note: FWFT is not stated explicitly but is implied by the stream semantics.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Single clock domain with rxd as the only asynchronous input. Active-low reset, async assert / sync deassert. txd and the synchronizer flops reset high.
key_decisions.plan_choice: Single domain with rxd as the only CDC point. Active-low async-assert/sync-deassert reset; txd resets high.

summary: The plan matches the reference closely on nearly every architecture decision. These include the shared 16x tick with a divider in cycles per tick, the 2-FF sync plus 3-sample mid-bit majority, start-bit re-verification, 10-bit RX FIFO entries with per-byte error sideband, drop-new with a sticky overflow, BREAK wait-for-high, early push at mid-stop, per-frame parity latching, back-to-back TX and the reset style. The only differences are minor and equivalent: a parameterized divider width, no tx_busy/rx_busy status (and so no busy-gated baud-change rule), an extra overflow pulse output, and the zero-divider policy left open. No questions were asked.
